current_mapping.description: describe the brief history and generations of computer;

stem: The generation of computers that started to use RAM and ROM for the first time is
explanation: Fourth-generation computers (1971–present), built around VLSI microprocessors, introduced semiconductor primary memory chips (RAM and ROM) to replace magnetic core memory.

option_feedback.reason: Second-generation computers used transistors and magnetic core memory for primary storage rather than semiconductor RAM/ROM chips.
Third-generation computers introduced integrated circuits (ICs), while widespread semiconductor RAM and ROM chips became standard in the fourth generation.
Fifth-generation computers focus on artificial intelligence, ULSI, and parallel processing long after RAM and ROM were already established.

stem: Computers that work on supply of continuous signals as input and display output simultaneously are
explanation: Analog computers process continuous physical quantities (such as voltage, pressure, temperature, or speed) and provide instantaneous real-time continuous output.

option_feedback.reason: Digital computers operate on discrete binary digits (0s and 1s) rather than continuous physical signals.
Hybrid computers combine both analog and digital components rather than operating purely on continuous signals.
Personal computers are general-purpose digital microcomputers that process discrete binary data.

stem: The type of computer that is MOST suitable to stream online videos is
explanation: Microcomputers (desktops, laptops, tablets, and smartphones) are designed for individual end-users and everyday multimedia tasks such as streaming online videos.

option_feedback.reason: Minicomputers (mid-range servers) are designed for multi-user departmental or industrial processing rather than personal media streaming.
Supercomputers are built for massive scientific simulations, weather forecasting, and nuclear research.
Mainframe computers handle millions of enterprise transactions for banks and airlines rather than individual video streaming.

current_mapping.description: describe input and output devices and their uses in daily life;

stem:
Some devices are essential to perform specific tasks on a computer.
Two essential devices to make a video call are
explanation: A video call requires capturing live video/audio and listening to the remote participant, which makes a webcam (video input) and headphones/headset (audio output/input) essential.

option_feedback.reason: A printer produces hardcopy paper output and has no role in real-time audio/video communication.
A scanner digitises flat paper documents into images and cannot capture live video or audio.
A scanner is a document-imaging input device rather than a live video capture camera.

current_mapping.description: describe types of sensors and their applications;

stem:
A system needs to automatically unlock the door in a house during the day and lock it at night.
The MOST suitable sensor to be used in this system is
explanation: A light sensor (photocell/LDR) detects ambient sunlight intensity, allowing an automated system to distinguish between daylight (day) and darkness (night).

option_feedback.reason: A pressure sensor detects mechanical force or weight applied to a surface rather than day/night cycles.
A moisture sensor measures humidity or water content in soil/air rather than ambient light.
A temperature sensor measures thermal heat, which can fluctuate independently of daytime or nighttime.

current_mapping.description: describe the components of Central Processing Unit (CPU) (Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), Control Unit (CU), Registers, Cache, and Internal Buses) and the role of each component in fetch-decode-execute cycle;

stem: A CPU contains all of the following components EXCEPT
explanation: The Central Processing Unit (CPU) consists of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), Control Unit (CU), and internal high-speed Registers; the input unit is an external peripheral subsystem.

option_feedback.reason: Registers are high-speed temporary storage locations built directly inside the CPU.
The Control Unit (CU) is a core internal component of the CPU that directs instruction execution.
The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) is a core internal component of the CPU that performs calculations and logical comparisons.

current_mapping.description: describe the components of Central Processing Unit (CPU) (Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), Control Unit (CU), Registers, Cache, and Internal Buses) and the role of each component in fetch-decode-execute cycle;

stem: A signal that causes data transfer from main memory to a CPU register is sent from
explanation: The Control Unit (CU) generates timing and control signals (such as Memory Read) over the control bus to coordinate data transfer between main memory (RAM) and CPU registers.

option_feedback.reason: The input unit transfers external user data into main memory under CPU supervision, not internal RAM-to-register control signals.
The output unit receives processed results from memory to display to the user.
The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) executes mathematical and logical operations on data already loaded into registers.

current_mapping.description: differentiate between primary (RAM, ROM, Cache) and secondary memory/storage devices;

stem: In contrast to RAM, one of the features of ROM is that it

options.A: can be increased in size to improve operational speed of a computer.
options.B: is used to store data, part of operating system (OS) currently in use.
options.C: is used to store BIOS and other data needed at start up.
options.D: can be written to and read from.

explanation: Read-Only Memory (ROM) is non-volatile firmware memory that permanently stores the Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) and bootstrap routines required to start up (boot) the computer.

option_feedback.reason: Upgrading RAM capacity—not ROM—improves multitasking and operational speed.
RAM stores the active portion of the operating system and currently running user programs.
Standard operation both reads from and writes to RAM, whereas ROM is primarily read-only during normal use.

current_mapping.description: differentiate between primary (RAM, ROM, Cache) and secondary memory/storage devices;

stem: Which of the following statements is FALSE about the cache memory levels?

options.A: Level 2 cache memory is located on the microprocessor.
options.B: Level 1 cache memory is located on the microprocessor.
options.C: Level 3 cache memory is slower than level 1 cache memory.
options.D: Level 3 cache memory is smallest in storage capacity than other two levels.

explanation: The official 2024 answer key accepts both D and A. This item is not used in single-answer practice.
answer_review_note: The board key accepts D and A; see the original answer key.

current_mapping.description: differentiate between primary (RAM, ROM, Cache) and secondary memory/storage devices;

stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE about hard disk drive?

options.A: It is a volatile storage device.
options.B: It is a primary storage device.
options.C: It uses optical disks to store data.
options.D: It uses random access method to access the data.

explanation: A Hard Disk Drive (HDD) is a non-volatile magnetic secondary storage device whose read/write heads move directly to any track and sector using direct (random) access.

option_feedback.reason: An HDD is non-volatile; it retains stored data permanently even when power is turned off.
An HDD is a secondary (auxiliary) storage device, unlike RAM which is primary memory.
An HDD uses magnetic platters coated with iron oxide; CDs, DVDs, and Blu-ray discs use optical storage.

current_mapping.description: describe input and output devices and their uses in daily life;

stem: The TWO most common output devices used on the billing counter of a supermarket are
explanation: At a supermarket Point-of-Sale (POS) billing counter, a monitor (screen display) shows itemized prices and totals while a thermal receipt printer outputs the printed customer bill.

option_feedback.reason: A keypad is an input device used for entering numbers/PINs, not an output device.
While a barcode scanner may emit a beep, a monitor and receipt printer are the two primary output devices displaying and printing the bill.
A keypad is an input device rather than an output device.

current_mapping.description: explain the following types of system software: a. operating system, b. device drivers, c. utility programs, d. language processors;

stem: The function that is NOT associated with an operating system is
explanation: Data analysis is performed by application software (such as spreadsheets, statistical packages, or BI tools), whereas resource allocation, process management, and memory management are core OS kernel functions.

option_feedback.reason: Resource allocation (assigning CPU time, memory, and I/O devices) is a primary operating system function.
Process management (scheduling, creating, and terminating processes) is a core operating system function.
Memory management (allocating and tracking RAM space for programs) is a core operating system function.

current_mapping.description: explain the following types of system software: a. operating system, b. device drivers, c. utility programs, d. language processors;

stem: The MOST common feature of user management systems is to
explanation: User management and security subsystems in an operating system maintain user accounts, authentication credentials, and Access Control Lists (ACLs) to enforce file and resource permissions.

option_feedback.reason: Process scheduling is handled by the OS process manager/scheduler rather than user account management.
Virtual memory management is handled by the OS memory manager using paging and swap space.
Network protocol handling belongs to the networking stack/communication manager.

current_mapping.description: explain the following types of system software: a. operating system, b. device drivers, c. utility programs, d. language processors;

stem: As compared to graphical user interface, the command line interface

options.D: uses mouse as an input device.

explanation: A Command Line Interface (CLI) renders only plain text prompts without heavy graphical windows, icons, or visual effects, so it consumes significantly less RAM and CPU resources than a GUI.

option_feedback.reason: CLI is harder for beginners to learn because users must memorise exact text commands and syntax.
Visual pull-down menus and toolbars belong to Menu-Driven and Graphical User Interfaces, not CLI.
CLI relies primarily on the keyboard for typing commands rather than a mouse.

current_mapping.description: explain the following types of system software: a. operating system, b. device drivers, c. utility programs, d. language processors;

stem: An essential component of a batch processing operating system is the
explanation: A batch processing operating system groups similar offline jobs together and relies on automatic job scheduling and queue management to execute them sequentially without user intervention.

option_feedback.reason: Batch processing executes queued jobs non-interactively without requiring live user interaction.
Interactive multi-tasking (time-sharing) switches rapidly among live user apps rather than running queued batch jobs.
Real-time processing algorithms belong to Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS) with strict deadline constraints.

current_mapping.description: explain the following types of system software: a. operating system, b. device drivers, c. utility programs, d. language processors;

stem: Which of the following options is a characteristic of a multi-user operating system?

options.A: It allows users to access the system simultaneously.
options.B: It cannot be used for personal computers.
options.C: It does not support system networking.
options.D: It requires less memory to operate.

explanation: A multi-user operating system (such as UNIX, Linux Server, or Windows Server) enables multiple users on different terminals or network sessions to access and share a central computer's resources simultaneously.

option_feedback.reason: Multi-user operating systems like Linux and macOS can also run on personal computers and workstations.
Multi-user operating systems extensively support and rely upon system networking.
Managing concurrent sessions and resources for multiple users requires substantially more memory, not less.

stem: If a person is working on an MS Word file, then the keyboard shortcut to open another new MS Word file is
explanation: In Microsoft Word, pressing Ctrl + N creates and opens a new blank document window.

option_feedback.reason: Ctrl + O opens the file browser dialog to open an existing saved document rather than creating a new blank file.
Alt + O is a legacy menu accelerator key rather than the shortcut for creating a new document.
Alt + N activates the Insert tab on the MS Word Ribbon rather than opening a new file.

stem: The shortcut key used to move the cursor at the beginning of the line is
explanation: Pressing the Home key moves the text cursor immediately to the beginning of the current line in a word processor.

option_feedback.reason: Alt + Home moves the cursor to the first cell in the current row of a table in MS Word.
Ctrl + Home moves the cursor to the very beginning of the entire document, not just the current line.
Shift + Home selects/highlights all text from the current cursor position to the beginning of the line.

stem: Which of the following menu tabs provides the option for applying header and footer to a document?
explanation: In Microsoft Word, the Header, Footer, and Page Number commands are located in the Header & Footer group under the Insert tab on the Ribbon.

option_feedback.reason: The Home tab contains clipboard, font formatting, paragraph alignment, and text style tools.
The Design tab contains document themes, colours, watermarks, page borders, and page background options.
The Layout tab contains page setup options such as margins, orientation, size, columns, and indents.

stem: Which of the following menu tabs provides the option for setting the margin of a document?
explanation: In Microsoft Word, document margins (Normal, Narrow, Moderate, Wide, or Custom Margins) are configured in the Page Setup group under the Layout (or Page Layout) tab.

option_feedback.reason: The Home tab handles font, paragraph, and clipboard formatting rather than page margins.
The Insert tab is used to add tables, pictures, links, headers/footers, and symbols.
The Design tab controls themes, page colour, and page borders rather than page margins.

current_mapping.description: explain the components of data communication (sender, receiver, message, transmission medium, and protocol) and modes of data transmission;

stem: The transmission medium can be defined as the

options.C: device to send or receive data.
options.D: rule to govern the data communication.

explanation: In a data communication system, the transmission medium (channel) is the physical cable or wireless electromagnetic pathway through which signals travel from sender to receiver.

option_feedback.reason: The information or data to be communicated is called the message.
The hardware device that sends or receives data is the sender (transmitter) or receiver (sink).
The set of rules governing data communication is called a protocol.

current_mapping.description: differentiate between asynchronous and synchronous data transmission modes;

stem:
Consider the given data to be transmitted via asynchronous transmission.
10101010
After adding start and stop bits, this data will become
explanation: In standard asynchronous framing (per the AKU-EB textbook convention), a Start bit of '0' is prepended before the 8-bit character (10101010) and a Stop bit of '1' is appended at the end, yielding 0 + 10101010 + 1 = 0101010101.

option_feedback.reason: Prepends '1' instead of the '0' start bit required to signal the start of a character frame.
Uses '1' as the start bit and '0' as the stop bit, reversing the start/stop framing convention.
Appends '0' at the end instead of the '1' stop bit needed to return the line to its idle state.

current_mapping.description: explain guided (twisted pair, coaxial, fiber optic) and unguided (radio waves, microwaves, infrared, satellite) transmission media;

stem: All of the following are advantages of using guided media in the data communication EXCEPT
explanation: Laying physical guided cables (especially fibre-optic and shielded cabling across buildings or trenches) involves high installation, cabling, and maintenance costs compared to setting up wireless unguided access.

option_feedback.reason: Guided cables contain the signal inside a physical conductor/fibre, providing lower attenuation than open-air wireless propagation.
Guided media such as fibre-optic and high-grade twisted-pair cables offer higher dedicated bandwidth than shared wireless links.
Fibre-optic guided media transmit light pulses and are completely immune to electromagnetic interference (EMI).

current_mapping.description: describe transmission impairments (attenuation, distortion, and noise/crosstalk) and communication performance metrics (bandwidth, data rate, baud rate, and SNR);

stem:
Consider the given table showing the picture of a digital signal sent from point A and received at point B.
The signal which is received at point B in this form is due to
explanation: Distortion occurs when different frequency components of a composite digital signal travel at different propagation speeds through a medium, warping the square waveform's shape at Point B.

option_feedback.reason: Crosstalk is unwanted coupling of a signal from one adjacent wire pair into another.
Attenuation is purely a loss of signal amplitude (strength) over distance without altering the waveform's phase shape.
Amplification strengthens the amplitude of a signal using a repeater or amplifier.

current_mapping.description: describe the functions of network communication devices (Modem, NIC, Switch, Router, Gateway, Access Point);

stem: A device that is used to access the internet via telephone line is
explanation: A dial-up modem (modulator-demodulator) converts digital computer data into analog audio signals to travel over standard public switched telephone network (PSTN) lines and demodulates incoming analog signals back into digital form.

option_feedback.reason: A router forwards data packets between different IP networks based on logical network addresses.
A switch connects multiple devices within a Local Area Network (LAN) and forwards frames using MAC addresses.
A Network Interface Card (NIC) connects a computer to a local network medium via Ethernet or Wi-Fi.

current_mapping.description: describe transmission impairments (attenuation, distortion, and noise/crosstalk) and communication performance metrics (bandwidth, data rate, baud rate, and SNR);

stem: Which of the following data transmission is measured in kilobits per second?
explanation: Data rate (bit rate) is the speed at which binary bits are transmitted over a channel per unit time, measured in bits per second (bps), kilobits per second (kbps), or megabits per second (Mbps).

option_feedback.reason: Baud rate measures the number of signal unit (symbol) changes per second (baud), not bits per second.
Analog bandwidth is the range of frequencies supported by a channel, measured in Hertz (Hz, kHz, MHz).
Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) measures signal power relative to noise power and is expressed in decibels (dB).

current_mapping.description: differentiate between primary (RAM, ROM, Cache) and secondary memory/storage devices;

stem: The number of bits in 8 bytes is
explanation: Since 1 byte equals 8 bits, 8 bytes contain 8 × 8 = 64 bits.

option_feedback.reason: 16 bits correspond to only 2 bytes (2 × 8 = 16).
32 bits correspond to 4 bytes (4 × 8 = 32).
128 bits correspond to 16 bytes (16 × 8 = 128).

current_mapping.description: explain the uses of computer networks, transmission modes (simplex, half-duplex, full-duplex), and network architectures (client/server, peer-to-peer, point-to-point);

stem: All of the following are the uses of a network EXCEPT
explanation: Word processing is a standalone application task (creating and editing text documents) that can be performed entirely offline on a single isolated computer without a network.

option_feedback.reason: File sharing across users and servers is a primary purpose of computer networking.
Electronic communication (email, instant messaging, VoIP, video conferencing) is a core function of networks.
Hardware sharing (sharing network printers, scanners, and storage drives) is a major benefit of networking.

current_mapping.description: explain the uses of computer networks, transmission modes (simplex, half-duplex, full-duplex), and network architectures (client/server, peer-to-peer, point-to-point);

stem: A transmission mode which sends data only in one direction is called as
explanation: In simplex transmission mode (such as television broadcasting, radio, or a keyboard-to-CPU link), communication is strictly unidirectional—one device only transmits and the other only receives.

option_feedback.reason: Full-duplex mode allows data to travel in both directions simultaneously.
Peer-to-peer is a network architecture in which nodes have equal privileges, not a directional transmission mode.
Client/server is a network architecture where clients request services from a central server.

current_mapping.description: explain the uses of computer networks, transmission modes (simplex, half-duplex, full-duplex), and network architectures (client/server, peer-to-peer, point-to-point);

stem: In a point-to-point network, the minimum number of device(s) that can be connected is/ are
explanation: A point-to-point connection establishes a direct dedicated communication link between two endpoints (one sender and one receiver), requiring a minimum of two connected devices.

option_feedback.reason: A single isolated device cannot form a communication link or network with itself.
Three devices form a multi-point or multi-node network rather than the minimum for a point-to-point link.
Four devices exceed the two-endpoint requirement of a point-to-point connection.

current_mapping.description: differentiate among types of networks: PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN, and Bluetooth networks;

stem: If a person creates a network with smartphone and shares the connection with his tablet, then the type of network is identified as
explanation: Connecting personal devices (such as a smartphone hotspot and a tablet) within an individual's immediate workspace (typically within 10 metres) forms a Personal Area Network (PAN).

option_feedback.reason: A Local Area Network (LAN) spans a room, office floor, or building connecting multiple workstations and servers.
A Wide Area Network (WAN) spans countries, continents, or the globe (such as the Internet).
A Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) covers an entire city or large metropolitan campus.

current_mapping.description: differentiate among types of networks: PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN, VPN, and Bluetooth networks;

stem: All of the following are uses of Bluetooth network EXCEPT
explanation: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless PAN technology (typically operating within 10 metres) using low-power radio waves; it cannot provide long-range wireless internet access across kilometres.

option_feedback.reason: Bluetooth is widely used to connect wireless keyboards, mice, and game controllers to computers.
Bluetooth is commonly used to stream audio to wireless headphones, earbuds, and speakers.
Bluetooth supports short-range peer-to-peer file transfers between smartphones and laptops.

current_mapping.description: describe network topologies (bus, star, ring, mesh, tree, and hybrid) along with their advantages and disadvantages;

stem: A topology which is MOST expensive among other topologies is
explanation: Mesh topology connects every node directly to every other node requiring n(n - 1)/2 dedicated cables and (n - 1) I/O ports per device, making it the most cabling-intensive and expensive topology.

option_feedback.reason: Bus topology uses a single shared backbone cable and is the least expensive topology to cable.
Star topology requires only one cable per node connected to a central switch/hub, costing far less than full mesh.
Ring topology connects each device only to its two immediate neighbours in a loop.

current_mapping.description: describe the functions of network communication devices (Modem, NIC, Switch, Router, Gateway, Access Point);

stem: A type of communication technology that provides the LOWEST internet connection speed is a/ an
explanation: A dial-up line transmits analog audio over standard voice telephone wires with a maximum theoretical speed of only 56 kbps, which is the slowest among all listed technologies.

option_feedback.reason: Digital Subscriber Line (DSL) provides broadband speeds ranging from several Mbps to tens of Mbps.
Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) cellular broadband delivers megabit-per-second mobile data speeds.
Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) provides digital channels of 64 kbps to 128 kbps or higher, faster than analog dial-up.

options.B: body attribute in the background tag.

explanation: In HTML, setting an image as the full-page background is done by placing the background attribute inside the opening <body> tag, i.e., <body background="image.jpg">.

option_feedback.reason: There is no <background> tag in HTML; 'body' is an element tag, not an attribute.
There is no <background> tag in HTML, and 'href' is used in anchor (<a>) and <link> tags.
There is no <href> tag in HTML; 'href' is an attribute of the <a> tag.

current_mapping.description: apply inline CSS styling (font-family, color, background-color, font-size, text-align) to HTML elements;

stem: Which of the following HTML codes should be used to display white text on a background having black color?

options.A: <body style="color: white; background-color: black;">Some text here</body>

explanation: Using inline CSS inside the <body> tag's style attribute, 'color: white;' sets the foreground text colour to white and 'background-color: black;' sets the page background to black.

option_feedback.reason: Wraps attributes in invalid quotes and uses the non-existent attribute 'fgcolor'.
Uses the non-existent HTML attribute 'backgroundcolor' (legacy HTML used 'bgcolor').
Uses the non-existent HTML attribute 'foregroundcolor' (legacy HTML used 'text').
